overview: Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn outlined her administration's priorities for the new term, focusing on departmental restructuring, infrastructure planning, and community health. Key initiatives include the transition to in-house parking management, the separation of diversity and human resources leadership roles, and the formation of a committee to pursue a new high school facility.

items.title: Zoning and Housing Priorities
items.summary: Mayor Lungo-Koehn outlined goals for zoning reform, the implementation of a housing production plan, and mixed-use development in Medford Square.

items.title: DEI and Human Resources Staffing
items.summary: The city has posted a position for a Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion Director after splitting the role from the Human Resources Director position.

items.title: Parking Management Transition
items.summary: The Mayor requested patience as the city transitions to in-house parking management and staff training following the expiration of the Park Medford contract.

items.title: Recreation and Rink Operations
items.summary: Discussion covered the activation of outdoor skating rinks and a pilot program for year-round operations at the LoConte Rink and Hormel Stadium.

items.title: High School Facility Planning
items.summary: The city intends to form a diverse vision committee to pursue state funding via the MSBA for a new or renovated high school facility.

items.title: School Safety and Behavioral Health
items.summary: The administration addressed school safety concerns and the formation of a Behavioral Health Committee to support student mental health.

items.title: Community Engagement and Events
items.summary: Residents were encouraged to participate in city boards, the master plan process, and planning committees for upcoming pride and multicultural events.
